name: CH592F
title: RISC-V microcontroller with Bluetooth LE 5.4, full-speed USB and segment LCD
summary: The CH592 and CH591 families are 32-bit RISC-V (QingKe V4C) microcontrollers with an integrated 2.4 GHz Bluetooth LE radio, a full-speed USB host/device with transceiver, a 12-bit ADC with PGA, touch-key sensing, a segment LCD driver, four 26-bit timers, up to four UARTs, SPI and I2C. A built-in DC-DC converter lowers running and radio current, and sleep modes go down to a fraction of a microamp. The CH592F is the QFN28 member with 448 KB of user flash, 26 KB of SRAM and 20 GPIO.
key_figures: 5.4, 1/2 Mbps, -95 dBm RX, -20 dBm to +9 dBm TX
3.4 mA typ with DC-DC at 80 MHz

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground, the 0 V reference. On the QFN packages it is the exposed pad underneath.

pins.name: PA10
pins.function: PA10 general-purpose I/O. Alternates: X32KI (input of the LSE oscillator, the other end of the 32 kHz crystal), TMR1 (timer 1 capture input 1 and PWM output 1).

pins.name: PB6
pins.function: PB6 general-purpose I/O. Alternates: RTS (UART0 modem request-to-send output), PWM8 (PWM channel 8), AIN9 (ADC input 9).

pins.name: PB0
pins.function: PB0 general-purpose I/O. Alternates: PWM6 (PWM channel 6), CTS (UART0 modem clear-to-send input), AIN8 (ADC input 8).

pins.name: VDCID
pins.function: Supply input of the internal LDO for the digital circuits. Needs a decoupling capacitor: 4.7 µF with the DC-DC converter on (1 µF to 10 µF works; a smaller value costs a little efficiency), 0.1 µF or more with it off.

pins.name: VSW
pins.function: Switching node of the DC-DC converter. With DC-DC on, an inductor placed close to the pin runs from VSW to VDCID: 10 µH recommended, 4.7 µH to 22 µH allowed (a smaller inductance lowers efficiency a little). With DC-DC unused, VSW ties straight to VDCID.

pins.name: VDD33
pins.function: Main supply input, from a battery or a regulator, which also serves as VIO33, the I/O supply, on every package. Decouple close to the pin: 2.2 µF or 1 µF with DC-DC on, 1 µF with DC-DC off. Its voltage is the VBAT channel the ADC and battery monitor read.

pins.name: PA6
pins.function: PA6 general-purpose I/O. Alternates: PWM4_ (PWM channel 4, remapped), RXD2_ (UART2 receive, remapped), RI (UART0 modem ring-indicator input), AIN10 (ADC input 10).

circuits.title: Supply with the DC-DC converter on
circuits.description: The CH592F in its QFN28 package running from one supply on VDD33, the converter enabled. An inductor from VSW feeds the VDCID node, which carries the digital LDO input and, tied to it, the analog LDO input VDCIA. Each supply node has its own capacitor to ground at the pin; the 32 MHz crystal sits across X32MI and X32MO, and the antenna connects straight to ANT.

parts.note: 4.7 µH to 22 µH allowed; close to VSW.
1 µF also allowed; close to VDD33.
0.47 µF to 2.2 µF allowed; close to VINTA.

notes: The HSE load capacitance is set inside the chip by RB_XT32M_C_LOAD, about 10 pF to 24 pF.
VDCID sits at 1.18 V to 1.38 V (1.3 V typical) once the converter runs.

circuits.title: Supply with the DC-DC converter off
circuits.description: The CH592F in its QFN28 package on direct power, the converter left disabled. VSW joins VDCID with no inductor, and VDCIA joins the same node; VDD33, VDCID, VDCIA and VINTA each keep their own capacitor to ground, at the values given for direct power.

circuits.title: 32 kHz crystal for the RTC
circuits.description: A 32 kHz crystal across PA10 (X32KI) and PA11 (X32KO) of the CH592F gives the LSE clock for the RTC. The two pins are left as inputs with no pull resistors, holding nothing but the crystal; the load capacitance comes from inside the chip.
notes: RB_XT32K_C_LOAD sets the internal load from about 12 pF to 27 pF.
Once the LSE runs, PA10 and PA11 stand at -0.3 V to 1.4 V at most.

operation.text: CH592X, CH592F, CH592A and CH592D carry 448 KB of CodeFlash, touch-key and I2C; the CH591F, CH591D and CH591R drop the touch-key and I2C blocks, have 256 KB of FlashROM in total and an ADC without DMA, and keep only UART0 and UART1. CH592X/F/D and CH591F run from 1.75 V; CH592A, CH591D and CH591R need 2.3 V. The CH592A is rated to 105 ℃ and has no page erase. The CH591R has no DC-DC converter.

QingKe RISC-V4C core, RV32IMAC plus vendor extensions, with a fast programmable interrupt controller and hardware stacking, branch prediction, single-cycle multiply and hardware divide. Flash runs essentially without wait states up to a 20 MHz system clock; the clock can go as low as 32 kHz. A 64-bit SysTick counts HCLK or HCLK/8.

512 KB FlashROM: 448 KB CodeFlash, 32 KB DataFlash, 24 KB bootloader and 8 KB InfoFlash. 26 KB SRAM in two blocks, RAM24K and RAM2K, each of which can stay powered through sleep. Programming is by ICP, ISP or IAP, and over the air. Flash erase and write go through vendor subroutines; CodeFlash reads through a pointer. Every chip has an 8-byte factory unique ID with checksum.
The PFIC, at base address 0xE000E000, handles up to 255 vectors; 19 peripheral and 8 core channels are in use, with one NMI and four fast vectors that jump straight to their handlers.

Six reset sources: power-on with low-voltage reset below Vlvr (RPOR), the RST# pin held low longer than Trst (MR), software (SR), watchdog (WTR and IWDG), the global reset on waking from shutdown (GRWSM), and a partial reset on waking from sleep (LRW) that clears only registers whose power was cut. R8_GLOB_RESET_KEEP survives every reset except RPOR and GRWSM. RST# is the PB23 alternate and is enabled by CFG_RESET_EN.
Registers marked RWA or WA accept writes only in safe-access mode: write 0x57 then 0xA8 to R8_SAFE_ACCESS_SIG; the window closes by itself after about 112 system clocks, or at once on writing 0x00.

VDD33 feeds internal LDOs for the flash, the digital logic (core, USB) and the analog blocks (HSE, PLL, ADC, radio); VIO33 powers the GPIO and flash. After power-on the chip runs on direct power. Turning on the DC-DC converter cuts running current to roughly 60 % of the direct-power figure; it needs the inductor and capacitors fitted first. In sleep the main LDO can hand over to an ultra-low-power LDO, keeping the PMU and RTC and optionally the RAM blocks, core, peripherals and LSE/LSI.
In safe-access mode set RB_PWR_DCDC_PRE, wait about 10 µs, enter safe-access again and set RB_PWR_DCDC_EN. To return to direct power, clear both bits in safe-access mode.

Idle stops the core with clocks running and wakes at once. Halt also stops the clock system; on wake the clocks restart before the core. Sleep turns the main LDO off and keeps PMU, core and basic peripherals on the ULP-LDO; after wake the LDO, then the clock, then the core restart and execution carries on. Shutdown keeps only the PMU (and selected RAM and 32 kHz clock); a wake event gives a GRWSM reset that software tells from a power-on reset by RB_RESET_FLAG and retained RAM.

Two ways to watch the supply: a low-power monitor costing about 1 µA with thresholds from 1.7 V to 2.4 V, or a high-precision detector with a low and an ultra-low threshold pair. Either can interrupt; enabling both low and ultra-low interrupts turns a threshold crossing into an NMI.

HCLK comes from the divided 32 MHz HSE, the divided 480 MHz PLL (HSE × 15) or the 32 kHz clock (LSE crystal or LSI RC). USB needs the PLL (48 MHz from Fpll/10); the RTC needs the 32 kHz clock on. LSI can be calibrated by software, counting it against the system clock, to about 0.1 %. The 32 MHz crystal is recommended for HSE and 32 kHz for LSE; both oscillators have internal adjustable load capacitors and bias current.

operation.topic: Switching the RTC to the LSE crystal
operation.text: Leave PA10 and PA11 as inputs with no pulls and nothing but the crystal on them. Power the LSE, start it at the highest bias current and drop to rated current once it has settled (a few hundred ms), then select it as CK32K; the switch completes after half a 32 kHz period, about 16 µs.

Independent counter powered with the PMU, so it keeps time through resets and low-power modes. Counters: 32 kHz cycles, 2 s units and days (16 bits each). Timing mode interrupts at a fixed period of 0.125 s to 16 s; trigger mode interrupts when the count reaches a preset alarm.

Up to 24 I/O on ports PA (PA4-PA15) and PB, each with selectable pull-up or pull-down and 5 mA or 20 mA drive. PB12-PB15 accept 5 V. Every I/O can interrupt on high level, low level, rising or falling edge and wake the chip; wake-up needs the pin interrupt and RB_SLP_GPIO_WAKE on. After reset all pins are GPIO; enabling a peripheral takes its pins, and where several alternates on one pin are enabled the one listed first wins. Ports are accessed in 8-, 16- or 32-bit words.
The two-wire debug interface uses PB15 (TCK) and PB14 (TIO) and is switched on or off by the ISP tool. While on, those pins serve only debug; while off, they are ordinary I/O.

Four independent 26-bit up-counting timers TMR0-TMR3 for timing, counting, capture and PWM. TMR1 and TMR2 can move capture or PWM data by DMA. PWM polarity is selectable and each value can repeat 1, 4, 8 or 16 times, which with DMA can mimic a DAC. Capture measures edge to edge (high or low width), falling to falling or rising to rising; bit 25 flags a result that timed out.
Eight 8-bit PWM outputs (PWM4-PWM11) with eight preset periods, or six 16-bit outputs (PWM4-PWM9) with a freely set period.

Four 16C550-style UARTs (two on CH591) with 8-byte FIFOs, 5 to 8 data bits, 1 or 2 stop bits, odd, even, mark, space or no parity, up to 6 Mbps. UART0 adds the modem lines, automatic CTS/RTS flow control, an RS485 transmit-status pin and hardware address matching for multi-drop buses. Outputs are 3.3 V LVCMOS and idle high.

One SPI, master or slave, modes 0 and 3, 8-bit frames MSB or LSB first, 8-byte FIFO and DMA. SCK reaches half of Fsys. Data is sampled on the SCK rising edge and changes on the falling edge. In master mode any I/O can serve as chip select.

One I2C (CH592 only), master or slave with multi-master, 100 kHz and 400 kHz, 7- or 10-bit addressing, dual 7-bit slave address, general call, arbitration, error detection, PEC, clock stretching and SMBus.

Drives up to 80 segments (20 × 4) at 3.3 V or 2.5 V, 1/2, 1/3 or 1/4 duty and 1/2 or 1/3 bias, from the 32 kHz clock. The LCD pins must be set analog-input-only and floating. SEG2 shares PB23 with RST, so using SEG2 means disabling the external reset.

The watchdog timeout reset counts 8 bits at 131072/Fsys. The independent watchdog IWDG runs from LSI with a 12-bit down-counter and prescaler 4 to 512; writing 0xAAAA reloads it, 0x5555 unlocks its settings, 0xCCCC starts it.

12-bit SAR ADC with 12 external channels (6 on CH591) plus VBAT and the temperature sensor; single-ended or differential, PGA gains from 1/4 to 16, an optional input buffer for high-impedance sources, input range 0 V to VIO33. Keep the buffer on unless the source impedance is under 1 kΩ; turn it off for differential inputs; it must be on for touch-key, with 0 dB (preferred) or -6 dB gain. Differential channel 0 measures AIN0 against AIN2, channel 1 AIN1 against AIN3; a result above 0x800 means the positive input is higher. Discarding the first conversion is recommended. CH592 adds DMA, timed automatic sampling and channel scan with an end-of-scan interrupt.
Read through ADC channel 15 with differential mode on, the buffer off and gain code 011b; averaging several readings improves accuracy.
Twelve capacitive channels on the CH592 working with the ADC, for key capacitances of 10 pF to 100 pF, with a shield drive output for sensitivity.

USB 2.0 host and device at 12 Mbps or 1.5 Mbps with on-chip transceiver needing no external parts; control, bulk, interrupt and isochronous transfers, 64-byte packets, 15 endpoints, DMA. In device mode an internal pull-up on the data line is enabled by register. UD+ and UD- are set as floating inputs.

2.4 GHz transceiver, baseband and link control with on-chip antenna matching and a single-ended RF pin; Bluetooth LE 5.4 at 1 Mbps and 2 Mbps, -95 dBm sensitivity, transmit power programmable from -20 dBm to +9 dBm. AES encryption, a two-channel DMA and four hardware timers for the link layer. The radio is driven through the vendor protocol-stack library.
Dimensions are millimetres; pin pitch is nominal and other dimensions are within ±0.2 mm.
